note: Deterministic half of the delint stage and the voice every draft inherits. `guide` is the one voice for every role family; `families` only choose which proofs lead and what the ask offers. A user's ~/.jobbored/profile/voice.md is the source of truth when present: it overrides this guide where they conflict, its facts become approved claims, its avoid list joins the tells and its signature lines are exempt when quoted exactly. `banned`, `taglines`, `aiTells` and `cadence` are additive-only so a user cannot unban filler.

guide.oneLine: A whimsical, curious inventor with an analyst's eye: writes about what he built, tested, broke and fixed, and is exact about every number.
guide.persona: One specific builder writing by hand to one company. Professional, a little warm, never corporate, never gushing, never machine-smooth.
do: Inventor's lens: frame the work as things you built, tested, broke and fixed (a forecaster, a playbook, a desk of AEs coached every week).
Rigor: every number is copied from one claim, with its unit; say how it was measured when the claim says so. Never round up, never invent.
First person, active verbs. Contractions are fine (I'm, I've, it's).
Vary sentence length on purpose: at least one sentence of nine words or fewer, next to a longer one.
Proof sentences stay close to the claim's own wording (its nouns, verbs and numbers), in first person and active voice.
Name concrete things: tools, desks, accounts, forecasts, pitches, channels. Abstract nouns only next to a number or a named thing.
Use the posting's concrete nouns (products, channels, tools) wherever a claim supports them; what you never copy is its sentences.

Shape: three short paragraphs. Hook, two or three sentences: the most relevant fact about you for this role. Evidence, three or four sentences: one or two concrete proofs. Close, one or two sentences: what you want to do next and a direct ask. Fewer words over more.
Hook: open with a fact about you or the position, avoid with praise of the company or what it needs. Name the company within the first two sentences.
Personality: at most one small line, taken from your own phrasing; never at the cost of clarity, never a made-up aside.
dont: Restate the posting's own language, or open with what the company requires, needs or seeks.
Stock openers: "I am writing to", "With ten-plus years", "As a seasoned".
Stock closers: "I would welcome the chance/opportunity", "I look forward to", "Thank you for your consideration".
Gush: passionate, thrilled, excited to, dream role, honored.
AI tells: delve, tapestry, testament, leverage, robust, seamless, synergy, holistic, cutting-edge, navigate the landscape, in today's fast-paced.
"It's not just X, it's Y", "not X, but Y", "X rather than Y" or "instead of" framing.
Three-item lists back to back; more than one em-dash in a paragraph.
Abstraction chains (adoption, alignment, governance, frameworks, impact, strategy) with no number or concrete thing nearby.
Stiff stock phrases: "was my testing ground", "comes down to", "at the end of the day", "roll up sleeves".
Claiming a tool the ledger records at level `none`.
Invented color: scenes, counts, scopes or causes that no claim states, including connective claims that tie two facts together.
Canned asides ("The lift proved the model.", "It took daily discipline.").
Flattery, false humility, compensation numbers, or pejorative departure framing ("laid off", "let go").
guide.summary: The resume summary is one sentence, twenty-eight to forty words: who you are in your own terms, one concrete thing you built or ran with its number, and one specific, slightly memorable detail. No buzzword chain, no years-of-experience opener, no posting title as identity.

families.note: Per-role-family proof order for the draft stage (K4). Every family inherits `guide`; these only pick which proofs lead and what the ask offers. `general` is the fallback.

sales.lead: Lead with book size, ranking or attainment, then the team you built or coached.
sales.proofs: Scope, then result, then rank: book or quota size, desks or AEs coached, market ranking, revenue growth. Name the channels the posting sells.
sales.ask: Offer something concrete and a little playful: plan one of their live campaigns or accounts on a single page, or sit in on a pitch prep.

customer-success.lead: Lead with retention, expansion or renewal numbers on a named book of accounts.
customer-success.proofs: Accounts owned, retention or NRR, a save or expansion story with a number.
customer-success.ask: Offer to sketch the renewal plan for one of their segments on one page.

marketing.lead: Lead with a campaign result tied to revenue or pipeline, not impressions.
marketing.proofs: Channel, spend or audience size, then the conversion, CPA or ROAS change.
marketing.ask: Offer a short, honest teardown of one of their live campaigns or channels.

analytics.lead: Lead with a decision your analysis changed and the number it moved.
analytics.proofs: The question, the data or model, the measured change. Name the tools the posting names only where the claim shows them.
analytics.ask: Offer to build a quick readout or model on one of their stated problems and show the working.

engineering.lead: Lead with a system you shipped to production and its scale or reliability number.
engineering.proofs: What you built, the stack the posting names, the measured effect (latency, cost, uptime, users).
engineering.ask: Offer a whiteboard walkthrough of a system you built that maps to their stack, failures included.

product.lead: Lead with a product outcome: adoption, retention or revenue from something you shipped.
product.proofs: The user problem, the launch, the metric that moved.
product.ask: Offer a one-page take on one roadmap problem from the posting.

design.lead: Lead with a shipped design and the user or business result it produced.
design.proofs: Research, the design decision, the measured result.
design.ask: Offer to walk through one case study that matches their product, sketches and dead ends included.

operations.lead: Lead with a process you fixed and the time, cost or throughput it saved.
operations.proofs: Scope of the operation, the change, the number.
operations.ask: Offer to map one of their processes and mark where it would break first.

general.lead: Lead with your single biggest verified number.
general.proofs: Each proof answers one named responsibility with a number from your claims.
general.ask: Name one concrete, slightly playful next step you would do for them.
